title: Living away from Earth
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the challenges of living in space, such as weightlessness, radiation and recycling air, water and food; both cover Earth's spheres and energy balance instead.

draft.title: Living away from Earth
card: In orbit, astronauts feel weightless because they and their spacecraft are falling around Earth together. Over time, weightlessness can weaken muscles and bones.
Beyond the protection of Earth's atmosphere, people are exposed to more radiation from the Sun and from space. Spacecraft need shielding to reduce this.
There is no air, water or food in space. A crew must carry these supplies or recycle them, as the International Space Station recycles much of its water.
Solving these problems is part of space science. Exercise routines, shielding and recycling systems all come from it.
draft.remember: Living in space means managing weightlessness, radiation and supplies of air, water and food.

a.q: Mei Ling is an astronaut on a long stay in orbit. Why does she exercise for hours each day?
opts: Weightlessness can weaken muscles and bones
Radiation makes her muscles grow too large
There is no air for her muscles to use
Recycled water makes her bones brittle
a.why: In weightlessness, muscles and bones do less work and can weaken, so exercise helps. Radiation is a real risk in space, but it is not the reason for this exercise.
a.clue: What happens when the body no longer works against its own weight?

b.q: A crew plans a trip to Mars that will last years. Why would recycling water be better than carrying all of it?
opts: It cuts the supplies the spacecraft must carry
It removes radiation from the drinking water
It lets the crew skip drinking water entirely
It makes the crew feel weightless for longer
b.why: Water is heavy and there is none in space, so recycling reduces what must be carried on a long trip. Recycling does not deal with radiation, and the crew still need to drink water.
b.clue: Think about how much a spacecraft must carry.

a.best: Weightlessness can weaken muscles and bones

b.best: It cuts the supplies the spacecraft must carry
